### Do Peer‑Mentoring Programs Help with Financial Aid? **Short answer:** Peer‑mentoring programs at Texas State are designed primarily to help you adjust to campus life, succeed academically, and connect with fellow students. They are **not** the official channel for processing or awarding financial aid, but many mentors are familiar with the **financial‑aid timeline, resources, and where to get help**. If you have specific questions about FAFSA, scholarships, loan repayment, or need assistance filling out forms, you’ll want to work directly with the **Financial Aid Office**. Below is a quick guide on how peer mentors can support you and exactly where to go for formal financial‑aid services. --- ## 1. What Peer Mentors Can Do for You | How a Peer Mentor Can Help | What They **Can’t** Do | |----------------------------|------------------------| | • Explain **when** aid is disbursed (e.g., tuition‑fee refunds in August, housing refunds in September). | • Approve or change your financial‑aid award. | | • Point you to **self‑service tools** like **BobcatGold** (your loan‑tracking portal). | • Submit FAFSA or Texas Application for State Aid (TASA) for you. | | • Share tips on budgeting, paying bills on time, and using the **Financial Education** resources offered by the aid office. | • Issue scholarships or grants. | | • Connect you to the **Financial Aid Office**, **Student Success Center**, or **Academic Advising** for more detailed questions. | • Negotiate repayment plans or deferments directly. | | • Offer moral support while you navigate the paperwork (e.g., reviewing a checklist you created). | • Access your **FERPA‑protected** financial‑aid record. | If a mentor doesn’t know the answer, they’ll usually refer you straight to a financial‑aid counselor. --- ## 2. Where to Get **Official** Financial‑Aid Assistance ### A. Financial Aid Office (Primary Contact) | What They Handle | How to Reach Them | |------------------|-------------------| | **FAFSA** & **TASA** submission help, verification, award letters, disbursement schedules, and troubleshooting. | **Phone:** +1 (830) 458‑4955
**Email:** financialaid@txst.edu
**Office Hours:** Mon‑Fri 8 a.m.–5 p.m. (in‑person at the Financial Aid Center, 115‑210 Caldwell Hall) | | **Scholarships** (Assured Scholarships, departmental awards, external scholarships). | Use the **Scholarship Search** on the Financial Aid website or ask a counselor for a list of eligibility criteria. | | **Loans** (FAFSA‑based federal loans, Texas‑specific loan programs, private loan counseling). | BobcatGold portal (log in with your Bobcat ID). | | **Grant & Gift Aid** (Texas Grants, Pell Grant, TEA awards). | Counselors can run a **“Aid Eligibility Check”** for you. | | **Financial‑Education Workshops** (budgeting, credit building, repayment planning). | Register via the **Financial Education** calendar on the aid site. | **Useful Links (from the sources you provided):** - **Applying for Aid:** https://www.finaid.txst.edu/applying/ – shows the Summer 2026 application portal and step‑by‑step instructions. - **Types of Aid:** https://www.finaid.txst.edu/typesofaid/ – explains federal, state, institutional, and private sources. - **BobcatGold:** Your personal loan‑tracking dashboard (login through the student portal). ### B. Supplemental Campus Resources | Resource | What They Offer | Contact | |----------|----------------|---------| | **Student Success Center** | Peer tutoring, academic coaching, and often a **Financial‑Aid Peer Advisor** who can walk you through the basics. | Phone +1 (830) 458‑4834 | | **Bobcat Promise** | Texas‑resident guarantee for tuition & fees (subject to eligibility). | Info on the Financial Aid site under “Bobcat Promise”. | | **Financial Education Workshops** | Free sessions on budgeting, credit, loan repayment, and FAFSA completion. | Register via the Financial Aid calendar. |
